messages:
Sophia Chen: FYI hitting a weird edge when requests include trailing slashes + duplicate query keys. upstream rejects signed requests if order changes. Is path canonicalization happening before header/query rewrites?

Mike Patel: path normalization runs in the matcher (we strip trailing slash and collapse repeated slashes), but query rewrites happen in the rewrite stage after matching. header injections/removals are applied during the proxy rewrite step. so order is matcher -> rewrites. :thinking:

Sophia Chen: That ordering is the problem. For tenant routing we rely on exact query order for signatures in a few legacy customers. If we dedupe/reorder queries in rewrite, signature fails. We need an explicit contract: canonicalize path, but do NOT touch query ordering unless a route enables dedupe.

Mike Patel: Agreed. We currently have a route option `normalize_query: true|false`. Default is true for new routes but legacy routes created before Jan 2025 are false. Might be a gap when routes are created via console vs API.

Angela Yu: Can we document an explicit precedence? Something like: 1) path canonicalization (strip trailing slash, percent-decode reserved characters) 2) route matching 3) header-level injections/removals 4) query rewrites (dedupe/sort) 5) final proxy to upstream. That makes the behavior predictable.

Bob Rivera: For header behavior, two asks: a) always remove any Authorization / Cookie headers when routing to internal telemetry or public upstreams unless route allows passthrough; b) inject `x-redwood-trace` with our trace id if not present. Also preserve X-Forwarded-For by appending.

Sophia Chen: Example flow I want (pseudo-config):
```
route: /v1/*
  match: exact (after path normal)
  rewrite:
    remove_headers: [Authorization, Cookie]
    inject_headers: {x-redwood-trace: "$trace_id"}
    query: {dedupe: false, sort: false}  # default false for legacy
```

Mike Patel: That looks good. Two notes: - `"$trace_id"` token is available at rewrite time. - We should support `append_headers` for X-Forwarded-For instead of replace.

Angela Yu: One more edge: we have a canary requirement where certain tenants (header `x-tenant: alpha`) need query dedupe on for performance reasons. We should support per-route overrides that match on header and flip rewrite behavior. Example: `overrides: [{when: header[x-tenant]==alpha, rewrite.query.dedupe=true}]`

Bob Rivera: Also ensure telemetry meters see the pre-rewrite URL path for attribution (i.e., emit both normalized_path and original_path). Otherwise costs/usage per-route will be wrong.

deploy-bot: deploy started to staging: deploy/2026-03-17T18:22Z :rocket:

Sophia Chen: Action items: 1) Mike — add explicit precedence doc and expose `preserve_query_order` on route API (owner) 2) Mike/Bob — default header sanitization rules for internal targets 3) Angela — add canary override UX in console (simple toggle + match) 4) Infra — ensure telemetry emits original_path + normalized_path.

Mike Patel: I'll draft the API change and a small migration plan (toggle to opt-in preserve_query_order) and propose a console UX change for route settings. Will post PR for API schema by EOD tomorrow.

Angela Yu: I'll mock the console panel and attach screenshots in a follow-up thread.

Bob Rivera: I'll add tests for header stripping + X-Forwarded-For append and a unit test that verifies signature-preserving behavior when preserve_query_order=true.

Sophia Chen: Thanks. One more: let's ensure we run a quick canary against 3 tenants that do signature checks before flipping globally. :thumbsup:
